title: Who is pretending?
summary: Narrate the creature demo with sense, think, act named at every turn, then take the honesty turn: when you say the robot is scared, who exactly is pretending, and can something act afraid without being afraid?
materials: the mBot creature and its line course
the state diagram page from Build
desk lamp for the sleepy trigger

steps.title: The honesty turn
steps.body:
This week you show the creature to the camera and narrate its mind. And the moment you say the words 'now it is scared', a trapdoor opens: is that true?

Here is what is true for certain. There is a variable called mood. When the distance reading drops under the threshold your own data chose, the variable flips to startled, the wheels reverse, the buzzer yelps. You built every piece, and your state diagram is the complete map of its so-called fear: nothing hidden, nothing left over.

So when the family gasps and says it is frightened, who exactly is pretending? Not the robot: pretending takes a pretender, and the diagram shows nobody home. Maybe you, the narrator, for choosing the word scared instead of saying a distance reading crossed a number. Maybe the audience, for playing along the way they play along with a puppet. Or maybe nobody is pretending, because acting afraid is a real thing all on its own.

That is the philosophy question of the week: can something act afraid without being afraid? A dog acts afraid of thunder and everyone calls the fear real. Your creature acts afraid of a hand and you wrote every line of the act. Where between those two does the line sit? Keep it simmering. Your talk ends on it, and the debate walks straight into it.

Voice rules, the same three as always: speak to the back wall, pause after the sentence that matters most, and look at one person per sentence.

steps.title: Prepare the creature narration
steps.body:
Two minutes, creature on its course, camera rolling. The shape of the talk:

Open on the diagram, not the robot. Hold the page up: three circles, four roads. Tell them this single page is the creature's entire mind, and that you will now demonstrate every road on it.

Then the live tour, with sense, think, act narrated at every turn. Roam: the eye under its chin reads the tape, the rule picks a wheel, off it goes. Your hand comes in: the distance eye reads a small number, the number crosses my threshold, the mood flips, it retreats and yelps. Lamp off: the light number dives, sleepy, snore. Button: awake. Name the sensor, the rule and the action every single time. The narration is the demo.

Close on the honesty turn, straight into the camera: when I said it was scared, the truthful version is that a distance reading crossed a number I chose. Then give your own answer, in your own words, to the question of the week: can something act afraid without being afraid?

Practise twice with a timer. The pause goes right after the yelp, while the family is still laughing: let the creature land the joke, then tell the truth about it.
checklist: Under 2 minutes, twice in a row
The state diagram page opens the talk before the robot moves at all
Every mood change got its sensor, its rule and its action named out loud
The talk ends with my own answer to the question of the week

steps.title: Steelman both sides
steps.body:
Tonight's motion is 'Robots can have feelings', and you do not enter the ring until you can argue both sides at full strength. That is the steelman rule, and this motion is exactly why it exists.

Strongest case for: nobody has ever seen anyone else's feelings, only their behavior. The dog acts afraid of thunder and we grant it real fear without demanding proof from the inside. If behavior is all the evidence we ever get, on what grounds does the creature's perfect little act count for exactly nothing? And feelings clearly come in sizes: a worm's alarm is simpler than a dog's, a dog's is simpler than yours. Maybe a three-mood machine holds the first millimeter of that staircase rather than standing off it entirely.

Strongest case against: with the creature, and only the creature, we hold the entire story: one variable, four roads, drawn on a single page, and every trigger was a number its builder chose. There is no inside left over for a feeling to live in. Calling the yelp fear is like calling a smoke alarm frightened of fire: the acting is real, but the actor is missing.

Write one sentence for each side, your best. Keep both in hand: whichever side you end up arguing, argue it like you mean it, with the state diagram as your exhibit.
checklist: One strongest-case sentence written for each side
Each sentence would make its own side proud, no strawmen anywhere
The state diagram is ready as evidence, whichever side gets to use it

steps.title: Record it
steps.prompt: Record the creature narration in one take: diagram first, all three moods triggered live with sense, think, act named at each one, and the honesty turn to close.
